newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chinese buyers make inquiries, rubber market dull.
newsitem.headline: Chinese buyers make inquiries, rubber market dull.

text.p: Chinese buyers were said to have made some inquiries by midsession on Friday, but business remained dull with little in the way of volume seen in the Singapore rubber market, dealers said.
"The Chinese submitted some inquiries, but they're probably just checking the prices. I don't think anything will get done," one dealer said.
Bridgestone, which asked for offers for SIR20 rubber over the past few days, was also out of the market, traders said.
"They just wanted to take a look at prices. I don't think anything was done with Bridgestone," another dealer said.
Sellers of SMR grade rubber were also trawling for buyers, but their offer price of around 282 Malaysian cents a kg remained out of the reach of most consumers, dealers said.
Traders said prices will probably drift lower now that wintering is almost over. "I heard production is coming up strongly," a trader said.

At around 0430 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 116.50-117.50 U.S. cents a kg from 117.50 cents. May RSS1 was indicated at 168.50 Singapore cents (US$1.17) a kg from 169.50 cents. May TSR20 was indicated at 158.25 Singapore cents a kg (US$1.10) from 159.25 cents. -- (US$1-S$1.43) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
